transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Time: 11:00 AM PT / 2:00 PM ET
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Marta Lopez (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhang (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (CTO, Nova Systems), Daniel Kim (Head of Infrastructure), Aisha Mensah (Security Engineer)

---
00:00 Marta Lopez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through Nova's security posture questions and make sure we cover Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options from a security and compliance point of view.
00:12 Priya Patel: Thanks, Marta. Yeah we, we moved this up the chain after an internal review. Primary concerns are certifications, SSO integration, and how keys and logs are handled.
00:23 Ethan Zhang: Great, quick intro from me, I'm Ethan on the infra and security side for Redwood, I'll handle the deep technical bits.
00:30 Daniel Kim: Cool. For context, we're evaluating for PII processing on our platform, probable HIPAA adjacent, not full PHI but close. We need to know the bounds for Hosted and when Dedicated or Private is required.
00:45 Marta Lopez: Understood. To start, Redwood's hosted API operates in our shared environment which is SOC 2 Type II compliant and we also have ISO 27001 certification. We can send both artifacts after the call. For dedicated and private we offer options to increase isolation and controls, e.g., dedicated GPU pools, private control plane, or on-prem.
01:05 Aisha Mensah: When you say "send artifacts" can you be specific  do you provide the full SOC 2 report, or an attestation letter? And do you have a pen test summary?
01:18 Marta Lopez: We typically provide the SOC 2 report under an NDA, and an SOC2 letter and summary for public consumption. We also include a recent third-party penetration test summary  the full pentest report is shared under tighter controls. I'll add that to the next steps.
01:34 Priya Patel: Good. On SSO  we use SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning and Okta as our IdP. How does Redwood integrate?
01:44 Ethan Zhang: Redwood supports SSO via SAML and OIDC and SCIM for user provisioning. For Hosted customers, you can configure SAML SSO and we support SCIM to provision RBAC groups. For Dedicated/Private deployments you can either use our managed IdP integration or we can plug into your IdP directly inside the customer VPC for Private. Authentication flows are normal web SSO; service-to-service tokens for API usage are still issued via Redwood's token system but we can map tokens to SCIM groups.
02:15 Daniel Kim: Are there options for just-in-time provisioning vs full SCIM push? We have contractors and want short-lived access.
02:25 Ethan Zhang: Yes, you can do JIT via SAML assertions and we also support short-lived session tokens and adjustable session TTLs. For Dedicated/Private, session policies can be enforced at the deployment level.
02:35 Priya Patel: RBAC  we need fine-grained roles, separation of duties, and auditability. Can you describe the role model?
02:44 Marta Lopez: Redwood's RBAC supports roles at org, project, and route/model level. Admin, Developer, Viewer are defaults; you can create custom roles and bind them to SCIM groups. Access changes are logged in audit trails.
02:58 Aisha Mensah: Where are the audit logs stored and for how long? We need 7 years for some workflows, but for now 2 years minimum. Also need immutable logs and export capability to our SIEM.
03:12 Ethan Zhang: Audit logs are retained according to plan. Hosted default is 90 days, with add-on retention packages up to multi-year. For Dedicated and Private, retention can be configured and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog or S3 exports. Immutable ledger-like retention depends on the deployment  on-prem you control that. We do support append-only logs and tamper-evidence in Dedicated with the right configuration.
03:38 Daniel Kim: Encryption  we want customer-managed keys (BYOK) and ideally HSM-backed. How does Redwood handle at-rest and in-transit encryption and KMS integration?
03:49 Ethan Zhang: At-rest encryption uses provider-managed KMS by default for Hosted. We offer BYOK (bring your own key) for Dedicated and Private; keys can be in your cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure KeyVault) and we support HSM-backed keys for higher assurance. For Private/on-prem we can integrate with your HSM over standard KMIP or cloud KMS proxies. In-transit is TLS 1.2/1.3 with mTLS option for Private deployments.
04:20 Priya Patel: Any constraints on model caching and KV cache  is any customer data written to persistent caches? We need to know if sensitive inputs are stored and for how long.
04:33 Ethan Zhang: Good point. By default, we enable ephemeral KV caches for inference and those are short-lived. For Hosted we have prefix caching that may keep tokenized prefixes for performance; those can be disabled. Persistent caches can be configured only in Dedicated/Private with explicit retention and purge policies. We can provide more detail in the architecture doc.
04:54 Aisha Mensah: Data residency  we have EU customers and some APAC, does Hosted guarantee region residency?
05:02 Marta Lopez: Hosted lets you pick region endpoints; we have EU-only data processing options and also offer Private deployments for strict residency. For Dedicated we can provision capacity in specific regions.
05:15 Priya Patel: Compliance with HIPAA  do you sign BAAs for Hosted or only for Private?
05:23 Ethan Zhang: We sign BAAs for certain enterprise agreements; typically Dedicated or Private is recommended for HIPAA scenarios, but Hosted can be used if contractual BAAs are in place and the deployment is configured properly. We'll need to pull legal's guidance  I'll flag that as an action.
05:40 Daniel Kim: Incident response and breach notification timelines? SLA for security incidents?
05:46 Marta Lopez: Our security policy includes 72-hour notification for confirmed breaches to customers by contract; we also have incident SLAs for Dedicated customers and can negotiate shorter notification windows in enterprise contracts.
05:58 Aisha Mensah: Logging again  can we push logs to our Splunk in near real-time?
06:04 Ethan Zhang: Yes, we support streaming logs to external SIEMs; near real-time depends on plan and throughput, but it's supported for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can use log export add-ons.
06:18 Priya Patel: What about customer data deletion  if we request deletion, how is model cache or logs removed?
06:25 Ethan Zhang: We support data deletion APIs and deletion workflows. For Hosted we have deletion SLAs (typically 30 days to purge from backups and caches). For Dedicated and Private we can meet shorter SLAs and we can run erasure jobs; for Private on-prem you control deletion fully. We'll include deletion SLA details in the docs we send.
06:45 Daniel Kim: Are there any common gotchas customers see moving from Hosted to Dedicated or Private? Performance, config drift, or extra ops?
06:53 Ethan Zhang: Main tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest to start but less isolation. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and more isolation but needs capacity commit. Private gives maximum control and residency but requires ops overhead. We provide deployment automation and ops runbook to minimize drift; SE-led onboarding helps.
07:10 Priya Patel: Is there a technical checklist for security review we can run through?
07:15 Marta Lopez: Yes we have a Security Review checklist that covers certs, network, IAM, KMS, audit logs, retention, penetration tests, and legal/contract items. I'll attach that.
07:25 Aisha Mensah: On SSO, do you support SCIM group sync for custom roles?
07:30 Ethan Zhang: Yes SCIM group sync maps to RBAC roles; we can do attribute mapping for fine-grained entitlements.
07:36 Priya Patel: For network isolation, do you support private endpoints and VPC peering?
07:41 Ethan Zhang: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink-like endpoints, and private control plane in Private deployments. For Dedicated we can do VPC isolation and private endpoints.
07:50 Daniel Kim: For KMS  will Redwood ever have access to plaintext keys? That's a big ask for us.
07:59 Ethan Zhang: Under BYOK, Redwood never sees plaintext private keys. We use envelope encryption where keys stay in your KMS; Redwood holds only wrapped keys and operates with decrypted data in memory within the runtime. For HSM-backed flows we can leverage KMIP or cloud KMS so Redwood doesn't manage raw key material.
08:20 Priya Patel: Excellent. A couple of quick follow-ups: 1) Can we run a small benchmark to confirm latency impact when BYOK/HSM is enabled? 2) Can we validate that audit logs include prompt/response metadata for forensics (masked as needed)?
08:36 Marta Lopez: Yes to both  benchmarks are common in pilots; we can run a small test harness. Audit logs include request metadata and we can mask sensitive fields and provide full context under strict controls.
08:48 Aisha Mensah: Would you be able to sign an NDA so we can share internal architecture and threat model?
08:53 Marta Lopez: Absolutely, we can sign NDA. I'll send an NDA template and the SOC2 docs under NDA.
09:00 Priya Patel: Timeline wise, we are aiming for a pilot in mid-October. We need to get security sign-off first.
09:07 Marta Lopez: Sounds good. We'll prioritize the docs and schedule a technical deep dive with Ethan and your infra team.
09:13 Daniel Kim: Also, pricing  does BYOK or log-forwarding add extra cost?
09:18 Marta Lopez: BYOK itself doesn't have a licensing fee generally, but some integration work and HSM carriers may incur one-time setup or management fees. Log-forwarding and extended retention are add-ons priced by volume. We'll include estimates in the follow-up pricing sheet.
09:35 Priya Patel: Great. Any objections from anyone?
09:38 Aisha Mensah: Nothing immediate, just need the details and to confirm deletion SLAs.
09:42 Marta Lopez: Ok recap and next steps: 1) I'll send SOC 2 and ISO artifacts + NDA, 2) Ethan will share architecture diagram and KMS integration notes, 3) schedule technical deep dive week of 10/4, 4) we'll prepare small benchmark plan for BYOK latency test.
09:58 Priya Patel: That works. Thanks everyone.
10:02 Marta Lopez: Thank you all, we'll follow up by end of day tomorrow with the docs.
10:07 Meeting ends.
